heart_rate.label: Heart rate
heart_rate.why_in_space: Weightlessness changes blood circulation and how the heart and blood vessels work. NASA's Human Research Program studies these cardiovascular adaptations.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep your regular measurement schedule.
guidance.attention: Rest for 10 minutes and measure again. Note anything unusual you feel.

bp_systolic.label: Blood pressure (systolic)
bp_systolic.what: Pressure in the arteries when the heart contracts.
bp_systolic.why_in_space: Part of the cardiovascular picture NASA monitors during spaceflight.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep your regular measurement schedule.
guidance.attention: Sit still for a few minutes and measure again.

bp_diastolic.label: Blood pressure (diastolic)
bp_diastolic.what: Pressure in the arteries between two heartbeats.
bp_diastolic.why_in_space: Part of the cardiovascular picture NASA monitors during spaceflight.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep your regular measurement schedule.
guidance.attention: Sit still for a few minutes and measure again.

glucose.label: Blood glucose
glucose.what: Amount of sugar in the blood.
glucose.why_in_space: A balanced diet is essential on long missions. NASA lists inadequate food and nutrition as a spaceflight risk.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep your regular measurement schedule.
guidance.attention: Note when you last ate and measure again later.

temperature.label: Body temperature
temperature.why_in_space: The stress of spaceflight can alter immune responses and reactivate dormant viruses (NASA Human Research Program).

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep your regular measurement schedule.
guidance.attention: Measure again in an hour and note any symptoms.

sleep_hours.label: Sleep
sleep_hours.what: Hours of sleep over the last 24 hours.
sleep_hours.why_in_space: NASA lists inadequate sleep and irregular schedules among the risks of long missions: they affect alertness, mood and performance.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep protecting your rest window.
guidance.attention: Protect tonight's rest window and log your sleep tomorrow morning. If it stays low, raise it at the next comm pass.

mood.label: Mood (self-reported)
mood.what: Self-assessment from 1 (very low) to 5 (very good). Not a clinical scale.
mood.why_in_space: Isolation, confinement and distance from Earth can take a toll on mental health. NASA tracks this as a behavioral health risk.

guidance.normal: Nothing to do. Keep checking in daily.
guidance.attention: Write a short note on how you feel. Talking with the crew or the support team on Earth is part of the routine, not an exception.
